bib.title: ASQA: Factoid Questions Meet Long-Form Answers

question: How can long-form QA be given a dataset and a well-defined correctness metric, by using ambiguous factoid questions whose answers must cover every interpretation?
hypothesis: A long answer is good if a user can answer each disambiguated question from it, so an automated metric built on that notion should agree with human judgments.
contributions: A crowdsourced dataset of long-form answers to 6,316 ambiguous factoid questions (ASQA).
An automated metric (DR), a human evaluation interface and a small human study showing agreement with DR.
Baselines combining joint passage retrieval (JPR) and T5-large, with a large gap to human performance.

method.summary: Annotators wrote paragraph-long answers to ambiguous AmbigQA questions, covering all disambiguated short answers and grounded in Wikipedia. DR combines ROUGE-L with Disambig-F1 (a SQuADv2 RoBERTa reader asked each disambiguated question over the generated answer). Baselines are DPR/JPR retrieval-only, T5-large closed book, T5-large open book on top-K JPR passages, an oracle and two human conditions.
method.task: long-form QA on ambiguous factoid questions (multi-document summarisation of retrieved Wikipedia passages)

datasets.name: ASQA (train)
datasets.source: Built on AmbigQA (itself on NQ-Open); crowdsourced long answers; Wikipedia grounded
datasets.preprocessing: 7,207 of 14,042 AmbigQA questions ambiguous; 417 with more than six disambiguations removed (6,790 left); 474 removed where annotators doubted the disambiguations; 6,316 remain

datasets.name: ASQA (dev)
datasets.split: dev; all Table 3 results are on dev

datasets.name: Human no-context annotation
datasets.source: annotators given only the ambiguous question

models.name: T5-C (closed book)
models.params: inferred: T5-large (size not given in a number)

models.name: T5-O-K (open book, K=1,3,5)
models.params: inferred: T5-large (size not given in a number)
models.architecture: T5 encoder-decoder, input = question + K JPR passages with wikipage titles, separated by '|'

models.name: ORACLE
models.architecture: T5 given question, short answers, disambiguated questions, context paragraphs and annotator's additional knowledge

models.name: DPR@1
models.architecture: BERT dual encoder trained on NQ

models.name: JPR@1 / JPR@K
models.architecture: reranker on top of DPR trained for multi-answer AmbigQA questions (Min et al., 2021)

other.note: Appendix B 'Parameter Choice' gives only context length and batch size; the fine-tuning recipe (T5-large size, lr, steps) is not stated.

inference.samples: not stated; Table 3 appears to be a single run per system
inference.prompting: No prompt text; input format is tagged fields (Figures 4 and 5 of the paper)
inference.retrieval: JPR top-K passages, K in {1,3,5}; random-retrieval baseline draws passages from the training set

metrics.name: ROUGE-L
metrics.definition: rouge-score 0.0.4, lowercased and Porter-stemmed; max over the two annotator references

metrics.name: STR-EM
metrics.definition: fraction of disambiguations whose short answer appears exactly in the long answer, per question then averaged

metrics.name: Disambig-F1
metrics.definition: RoBERTa SQuADv2 reader answers each disambiguated question over the generated answer; token F1 against the gold short answer, averaged within then across questions

metrics.name: Human ACC
metrics.definition: average fraction of disambiguations a human verifies can be answered from the answer

metrics.name: Human pairwise COMP / FLUE / HO
metrics.definition: pairwise comparisons; 1 point for a win, half for a tie, divided by the number of comparisons

eval.protocol: Automated metrics on the dev set. Human study: 45 random dev questions, 4 model outputs plus 2 human sets, split into three pairs per question, judged blind by the paper's authors. Pearson correlations of system-level scores with human metrics. No seeds or significance tests for model results.

results.quote: While the difference with Disambig-F1 is not statistically significant

limits: Disambig-F1 and STR-EM measure recall only; hallucinated extra disambiguations may keep scores high and are penalised only indirectly via ROUGE-L and distractors degrading the reader (Section 9).
Inter-annotator agreement may be inflated by the shared AmbigQA disambiguations (Section 9).
Disambig-F1 needs a strong QA reader; off-Wikipedia domains may need fine-tuning of the RoBERTa SQuADv2 model (Section 9).
Human study is small: 45 questions, 6 systems, judged by the paper's authors; DR vs Disambig-F1 not significantly different.
Disambig-F1 underestimates human ACC (distribution shift, distractors), though ordering is preserved (r=99.3).
T5 training details (size, lr, steps, decoding) are not given; baselines are 2022 T5-large, long dated by LLMs.
ASQA is much smaller than ELI5 and MS-NLG.

fraction of disambiguations for which the short answer is present in the long answer (exact match)
